segments.description: Sermon on Divine Perfection, overcoming fear, and the power of praise.

content.text: By the grace of God. October is our month of divine perfection. The Lord will perfect all that concerns you. We see in Psalms 138:7-8 that God’s mercy is everlasting. In 2 Chronicles 20, Jehoshaphat faced a great army, but God told him not to be afraid or discouraged. When we praise God, even before the battle is won, we show our faith. Divine perfection is not about our ability, but about God’s mercy and our willingness to praise Him. When opposition comes, it is an opportunity for God to show His power. Let us trust God, pray, and praise Him in every season, knowing He perfects all that concerns us.

segments.speaker: Pastor Benjamin
segments.title: Divine Perfection
segments.summary: The sermon emphasized that divine perfection is achieved not by our own strength, but through God's mercy and our praise. Drawing from Psalms 138 and 2 Chronicles 20, the message encouraged believers to overcome fear and anxiety by seeking God in prayer and worship, trusting His promises, and praising Him even before victory is visible. The congregation was reminded that opposition is an opportunity for God to demonstrate His power, and that praise is both a weapon and a sign of faith. The sermon concluded with a call to reflect on God's faithfulness and to rejoice in every season, knowing that God perfects all that concerns His children.
